blocking.section: Budget philosophy (Budget catalog and SLO ties); Benchmark methodology (Scenarios); Benchmark suite and CI gating (Suite layers; Constants the suite verifies)
blocking.issue: The overload scenario O1 cannot reach the in-flight ceiling or emit RZ-RT-005, so PB-11 and the 20,000 in-flight constant are unverifiable, and every O1 run fails the document's own validity rule. O1 is S1, which has 256 HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections. At most 256 requests can therefore be in flight. With a mock whose p99 is 200 µs, Little's law gives about 50 in flight at 50,000 rps. At 150% offered load, the excess 25,000 rps waits inside the generator, where latency correction records it as latency. The Node never sheds it. The achieved rate misses the offered rate by about 33%, so the 0.5% validity rule rejects every O1 run. The scenario also contradicts 'Budgets hold on RH-1 only', because O1, C1 and R1 gate on 'Dedicated runners'. Failure scenario: at 10x load the real 20,000-unit shedding path, never queued, runs untested for the first time in production.
blocking.evidence: L84 'PB-11 | Goodput with S1 offered at 150% of saturation | 90% or more of saturation throughput, excess rejected only as `RZ-RT-005` (target)'; L281 'S1 | GET, 1 KiB response from the mock, 256 keep-alive connections (target)'; L488 'In-flight units per Node | 20,000 (target) | Data plane | O1: `RZ-RT-005` at the ceiling, never queued'; L370 'A run is valid only if the achieved rate stays within 0.5% of the offered rate (target)'; L154 'Budgets hold on RH-1 only'; L416 'Scale | C1, O1, R1, F1 (SM-9), SM-10 | Dedicated runners'.
blocking.fix: Define O1 as its own workload rather than 'S1 at 150%'. Use at least 25,000 client connections, or HTTP/2 on 8443 with 100 connections of 250 streams. Delay the mock by 500 ms (target) so that 40,000 rps × 0.5 s fills the 20,000 in-flight units. Offer 150% of that rate. For O1, validity means that admitted responses plus RZ-RT-005 responses match the offered rate within 0.5% (target). Pass when goodput is at least 90% (target), no request waits before its RZ-RT-005, and RZ-RT-005 responses are written with p99 of 1 ms or less (target), counted from `ruralz_http_active_requests` and `ruralz_http_listener_requests_total`. Run O1, C1 and R1 on RH-1 hosts, or state that their budgets gate only there.

blocking.section: Benchmark suite and CI gating (Constants the suite verifies)
blocking.issue: The test assigned to the State Store in-flight ceiling cannot reach 8,192 calls, so the overflow path ('an excess call is skipped under failureMode') is never exercised. S5 is 'As S1', which caps concurrency at 256 requests, and each request makes at most one blocking call. The Policy's `stateStoreTimeout` falls back to the Gateway default, which Scalability advises at 5 to 10 ms, so callers stop waiting after about 10 ms. That caps the rate near 25,600 rps. By Little's law, 25,600 rps × 0.2 s is about 5,120 calls in flight. A 200 ms fault also makes calls time out, and the per-shard breaker then opens ('50% of at least 20 calls in 5 s fail') and skips calls, so the in-flight count falls further. Failure scenario: in a real 10x brownout with thousands of concurrent requests, the ceiling, and the goroutine and memory behavior at it, run for the first time in production.
blocking.evidence: L493 'State Store calls in flight | 8,192 (target) | Scalability and distributed state | S5 with 200 ms added latency (target), CE-3'; L285 'S5 | As S1 | `ratelimit` on the `redis` driver'; Scalability State client: 'at most 8,192 blocking calls in flight (target), each counted until its reply or a connection reset, not its caller's timeout' and 'A per-shard breaker opens when 50% of at least 20 calls in 5 s fail'.
blocking.fix: Add a dedicated scenario of about 12,000 concurrent requests, reusing C1's connections. Set `stateStoreTimeout: 1s` on the bench `ratelimit` Policy; the field is defined in the Configuration model. A fault proxy adds 200 ms (target) and returns no errors, so the breaker stays closed. Pass criteria, each (target): in-flight calls plateau at 8,192; the excess is skipped under `failureMode` and counted in `ruralz_state_calls_total`; the goroutine count stays bounded; skipped requests add no more than 1 ms at p99. Add an Open question to Observability for an in-flight State Store call gauge, because none exists in the catalog.

blocking.issue: S2 and S5 rate-limit a single hot key, which contradicts Scalability's hot-key rule and leaves the key table and shard distribution unexercised. The bench key is `source.ip`, and all load comes from the single load generator host RH-1L. Every request therefore hits one key: 40,000 GCRA calls per second on one key and one shard in S5. That is above the 25,000 per second at which Scalability says a key 'MUST use `localOnly` mode'. The run never exercises key-table CLOCK eviction, the first-seen budget, the over-limit cache or hash-slot spread. PB-9 and the S5 throughput row therefore measure a pathological single-key case that the design forbids, not a production key mix.
blocking.evidence: L357 'key: "source.ip"'; L358 'limits: [{requests: 1000000, window: 1s}]'; L159 'RH-1L, RH-1U | Load generator host'; L175 'S5 GCRA in a `redis` State Store | 40,000 rps or more on the Node (target)'; Scalability Distributed rate limits: 'A key whose `requests` exceed 25% of one shard's calls, about 25,000 per second (hypothesis), MUST use `localOnly` mode'.
blocking.fix: Derive the bench key from a header, `key: 'request.headers["x-bench-key"]'`, using the CEL `request.headers` variable of the Configuration model. The generator should cycle 100,000 distinct keys (target), uniform in S2 and S5, plus a Zipf variant that keeps the hottest key under 25,000 calls per second (target). Record the key cardinality and distribution in the result record. Keep a separate single-key run only as the CE-12 hot-key check.

blocking.section: Throughput and resources per core (Throughput targets)
blocking.issue: No scenario measures the per-shard GCRA throughput hypothesis that Scalability's Cell sizing rests on. BP-1 promises that the first benchmark to measure a hypothesis turns it into a target, but S5 drives one 4-vCPU Node at 40,000 rps, at most 40% of the assumed 100,000 calls per second per shard. The document itself says no published EVAL throughput exists, and the research confirms that. Scalability derives four things from this number: the 1,000,000 calls per second Cell ceiling, the 25,000 per second hot-key threshold, the 200-Node binding point and the connections-per-shard limit. Failure scenario: if Lua GCRA on one Valkey main thread saturates at, say, 40,000 calls per second, every Cell sized from this document overloads its shards at 2.5x lower load. Breakers then open Cell-wide and Rate Limits fail open at N_serving × ceiling.
blocking.evidence: L175 'about 100,000 GCRA calls per second per shard (hypothesis)'; L180 'S5's per-shard figure is a hypothesis: no published EVAL throughput exists'; L48 'The first benchmark that measures a hypothesis turns it into a target or changes the design'; Scalability Cell sizing: 'State Store calls per second per Cell | 1,000,000, 62.5% of 16 shards at about 100,000 each (hypothesis)'; research scalability-patterns.md: 'no Lua/EVAL (GCRA-style script) throughput per core was found'.
blocking.fix: Add a shard-saturation scenario, Planned (M1). Drive one Valkey primary on its own host with a fixed cpuset, using an open-loop generator of GCRA `EVALSHA` calls through the State client, or several Nodes. Step the rate until the p99 round trip exceeds 1 ms or script CPU reaches 70% (target). Include 10 × N connections per shard as a variant. Publish calls per second per shard at 70% script CPU as the coefficient Scalability and Capacity planning consume, and add it to the milestone plan and to the Capacity planning hand-off in Reporting.

blocking.section: Budget philosophy (Budget catalog and SLO ties); Benchmark methodology (Scenarios)
blocking.issue: The document ignores cross-zone State Store latency even though the recommended deployment pays it. Scalability says a Cluster SHOULD span at least two zones and keeps a single primary with a replica in another zone. Nodes outside the primary's zone, and every Node after a zonal failover, therefore pay the 2 ms cross-zone p99 (hypothesis). PB-9 and S5 measure only the same zone. Yet BP-3 says a budget uses 'the same metric and threshold as a production SLO', and SLO-GW-5 counts every `op="gcra"` call against 1 ms, with no zone split. Failure scenario: in the recommended 2-zone topology, about half of all GCRA calls take about 2 ms. SLO-GW-5 then burns continuously in production while the lab gate passes, and a zonal failover sends all calls cross-zone with no budget or benchmark behind it.
blocking.evidence: L82 'PB-9 | Same-zone GCRA round trip p99 | 1 ms or less (hypothesis) | ... | SLO-GW-5'; L285 'a Valkey primary in the same zone'; L50 'BP-3 | A Performance Budget is the lab ceiling on the same metric and threshold as a production SLO'; Scalability Latency budgets: 'Cross-zone State Store round trip in one Region, p99 | 2 ms or less (hypothesis)'; Scalability: 'A Cluster SHOULD run at least three Nodes in at least two zones (target)'.
blocking.fix: Add a cross-zone S5 variant, with the Valkey host in a second zone or with injected round-trip time, and a budget PB-9x: cross-zone GCRA round trip p99 of 2 ms or less (hypothesis), matching Scalability. Also add an Open question owned by Observability: should SLO-GW-5 restrict its SLI to same-zone calls, or take a zone-relative label, so that the SLO and PB-9 measure the same population?

blocking.section: Per-stage latency budget; Throughput and resources per core (Throughput targets)
blocking.issue: PB-2 and PB-3 hold only at half of S2 saturation, but Scalability's sizing rules run Nodes above that load, so no budget covers gateway-added latency at those loads. In steady state the autoscaling threshold allows 53% CPU with three zones and 60% with four. After a zone loss, the survivors run at up to 80% CPU by design. SLO-GW-2 is tied to PB-2 and applies at every load. Failure scenario: a zone is lost in a 3-zone Cluster, and the survivors run S2-like traffic at about 80% utilization. The document gives no p99 at that point, and its own queueing note suggests p99 exceeds 1 ms there. SLO-GW-2 then burns during exactly the incident the HA rules were sized for, and no lab gate would have predicted it.
blocking.evidence: L75 'PB-2 | Gateway-added p99, S2 reference scenario at half saturation (SM-4) | 1 ms or less (target)'; L172 'PB-2 and PB-3 at half saturation (target)'; L163 'queueing at 80% utilization alone would push p99 past 1 ms (hypothesis)'; Scalability Autoscaling signals: '80% × (Z − 1) / Z ... 40% at two, 53% at three, 60% at four (target)'; Scalability Ruralz Gateway availability: 'sized so that losing the largest zone keeps survivors under 80% CPU (target)'.

Examples: p99 of 2 ms or less (target), gated in the saturation ladder job, and a p99 at 60% of saturation, the steady-state autoscaling ceiling. State whether SLO-GW-2 counts zone-loss periods against its error budget, and add an Open question to Scalability if the autoscaling thresholds must drop to the load where PB-2 is proven.

blocking.section: Startup and reload time by configuration size (Fleet-level timing); Benchmark suite and CI gating (Statistics and runners)
blocking.issue: No scenario, runner or gate verifies the fleet-scale budgets. Control plane and GitOps says Performance budgets and benchmarking measures the 10,000-Node largest batch. The only fleet scenario is F1, with 100 `ruralzd` processes. blocking.section: Benchmark suite and CI gating (Constants the suite verifies)
blocking.issue: The constants table verifies only a subset of the ceilings that dependency documents delegate to this suite. Scalability says this document 'verifies every value' in its Per-node limits table, and Data plane says the suite verifies its 'Bounded resources ceilings'. The table has no test for any of these: buffered bytes (512 MiB, RZ-RT-004), the local-only key segment (131,072), the Quota denial cache (65,536), the first-seen GCRA budget, balancer structures (256 MiB), the Response Cache hot-entry layer (64 MiB), State Store connections per shard (2 + 8), HTTP/2 streams per connection (250), the 2,000 concurrent pre-routing rejection writes, and the worst-case per-connection memory of 592 KiB. The 'Worst-case Node' row (about 19 GiB) is an unmeasured hypothesis. The rate-limit key table row also names the wrong owner: Scalability names Traffic management. Failure scenario: under a 10x slow-client or body flood, these unverified ceilings decide whether a Node rejects work or is OOM-killed.
blocking.evidence: Constants table L483-494 lists 8 rows only; L491 'Rate-limit key table | 1,048,576 entries, about 64 MiB (target) | Scalability and distributed state'; L228 'Worst-case Node | About 19 GiB plus snapshots, fitting a 32 GiB Node (hypothesis) | Data plane'; Scalability Per-node limits: '[Performance budgets and benchmarking] verifies every value' and 'Rate-limit key table | ... | [Traffic management]'; Data plane Performance budgets: 'Its suite also verifies this document's constants: Bounded resources ceilings, K and the grace period'.
blocking.fix: Add one compact row per delegated ceiling, naming its test. Examples: a body flood to `limits.maxBufferedBytes` with RZ-RT-004 and no OOM; CE-15 for the local-only segment; a slow-header and HTTP/2-window flood over 20,000 connections measuring worst-case per-connection RSS against 592 KiB (hypothesis); 2,000 or more pre-routing rejections. Correct the key-table owner to Traffic management and resilience. Put rows that cannot run in M1 in an Open question rather than leaving them silent.

blocking.issue: The memory rows cannot all hold together, because the base leaves no room for the label sets placed 'inside' it. 95 MiB is 99,614,720 bytes, which leaves 385,280 bytes of the 100,000,000-byte PB-6 base. The table nevertheless places 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes) of sharded label sets 'inside the base', and bills the per-Route slope separately at 2 KB. At R = 1,000, 99,614,720 + 2,097,152 + 2,000,000 is 103,711,872 bytes, above PB-6's 102,000,000. The pr-full idle-RSS gate at 95 MiB can pass while PB-6 fails at every Route count up to about 17,000, so the Capacity planning memory coefficient is wrong at scale.
blocking.evidence: L211 'PB-6 compares bytes: 100,000,000 plus 2,000 per Route (target)'; L215 'Idle RSS, no Revision, telemetry at defaults | 95 MiB or less (target)'; L217 'Per-Route slope between 1,000 and 17,000 Routes | 2 KB or less (target)'; L218 'Sharded label sets of the first 1,000 admitted Routes | 2 MiB or less at 4 stripes (target), inside the base'.
blocking.fix: Make the arithmetic close. One option: set idle RSS to 93 MiB (target), about 97.5 MB, leaving 2.5 MB for the sharded sets. Another: charge the sharded sets to the slope and fit it only above 1,000 Routes, with a separate first-1,000 allowance. Show the byte sum at R = 1,000 and R = 17,000 in one sentence, and keep OQ-performance-budgets-and-benchmarking-5 and -10 consistent with the chosen option.

blocking.section: Throughput and resources per core (Resources per core); Memory budget
blocking.issue: No budget covers a client connection storm on the Nodes that survive a Node or zone loss. Clients of a lost Node or zone reconnect to the survivors with fresh TLS handshakes. At the document's 2,000 handshakes per second per vCPU (hypothesis), a 4-vCPU Node needs about 2.5 s of all its CPU to accept 20,000 connections, while it keeps serving existing traffic. No scenario measures the p99 of existing traffic, or the handshake latency, during such a storm. On memory, 20,000 TLS connections at 96 KiB need about 1.9 GiB, far above the 256 MiB loaded budget and the 512 MiB container of the informational `GOMEMLIMIT` run. The document never states the container memory the default 20,000-connection ceiling requires. Failure scenario: survivors in right-sized containers run into `GOMEMLIMIT` GC thrash or an OOM kill before they reach the connection ceiling. Their clients move on to the next survivors, and the failure cascades.
blocking.evidence: L194 'New TLS 1.3 handshakes, ECDSA P-256 | 2,000 or more per second per vCPU (hypothesis)'; L222 'Idle HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 connection over TLS | 96 KiB or less (target) | 20,000 fit in about 1.9 GiB (target)'; L225 'Loaded RSS, S1 at 40,000 rps with 256 connections | 256 MiB or less (target)'; L230 'An informational run adds `GOMEMLIMIT` at 90% of a 512 MiB container limit (target)'; Scalability CE-1 checks only 'Errors only on its in-flight requests'.
blocking.fix: Add scenario C2, Planned (M1). Run S3 at half saturation, then open 10,000 new TLS connections within 2 s (target). Budget the existing traffic's p99 during the storm (for example 5 ms or less (target)) and the p99 of `ruralz_listener_tls_handshake_duration_seconds`. Add a Memory budget row for the minimum container memory at the default ceilings (for example 20,000 × 96 KiB + 256 MiB, about 2.2 GiB (target)). Run the `GOMEMLIMIT` variant under C1 plus S2, so the limit actually binds, and report GC CPU.
